narrativeBlocks.title: The scene
narrativeBlocks.body: In Budge's translation of Chapter 125, the deceased addresses named judges and declares that they have not committed particular wrongs. The text frames judgment as a speech act before divine assessors.

narrativeBlocks.title: A few declarations from Chapter 125
narrativeBlocks.body: Source quotation (Budge translation; whitespace normalized): “Hail, thou of the long strides, who comest forth from Heliopolis, I have not committed sin. 2. "Hail, Crusher of bones, who comest forth from Hensu, I have not lied.”

narrativeBlocks.title: Why it matters
narrativeBlocks.body: These declarations belong to a particular funerary text and edition. Do not turn them into one uniform moral code for every Egyptian person or period.

narrativeBlocks.title: Read the evidence carefully
narrativeBlocks.body: The source is a translated collection with editorial explanations. A text about judgment is evidence for this ritual-literary tradition, not direct observation of every funeral practice.

narrativeBlocks.title: Carry it forward
narrativeBlocks.body: When a funerary text speaks in the first person, ask whether the speaker is the deceased, a ritual officiant, or a god.
